content:
The Clay plugin has two halves: the Clay CLI for scripting and ephemeral operations, and a local MCP server that exposes Clay’s tools to a coding-agent host such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor. Installing the plugin wires up both. The plugin needs a coding-agent host that can run `clay mcp` as a local process, call its tools, and also run the `clay` CLI directly — Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor all support this. General-purpose chat apps like Claude Desktop, claude.ai, and ChatGPT can call MCP tools, but they have no shell tied to the session, so they can’t run the `clay` CLI.

##
​

How it works

An MCP host spawns `clay mcp`, which runs as a long-running server over stdio and forwards the host’s tool calls to Clay. It authenticates with the same credentials as the rest of the CLI — the session from `clay login`. You do not put an API key into the host config. The server resolves its session once at startup, so if you sign in after it launches, restart your agent so its MCP server picks up the new session.

##
​

Workspace pinning

Because the server resolves its session once at startup, an MCP connection stays pinned to whichever workspace was active then — re-running `clay login` only updates the credential on disk. To switch workspaces, sign in to the new workspace and have the host restart the server so it picks up the new credential.

##
​

CLI or MCP

Use the MCP server when an agent host should call Clay’s tools as part of its normal tool-use loop. Reach for the [CLI](/quickstart#agent-plugin) for one-off runs, scripting, and inspecting data from a shell, and the [Public API](/quickstart#api) when you are building a service or app that calls Clay programmatically.
